chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was praying, so the Imam came out, and the man had already prayed one rak'ah from an obligatory prayer. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was a just Imam, let him pray another (rak'ah) and finish, and he should make these two voluntary (prayers), and let him enter with the Imam in his prayer, just as he is.'

And if he is not a just Imam, let him build upon his prayer, just as it is, and he should pray another rak'ah with him, sitting, for the duration of saying: 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). Then let him complete his prayer with him, according to what he is able to, for dissimulation (taqiyyah) is vast, and there is nothing from dissimulation except that its performer is recompensed upon it, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they have already prayed an obligatory prayer individually and the Imam comes out to lead the congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the jurisprudential procedure for a worshipper who has completed an obligatory prayer individually before the Imam leads the congregational prayer. It distinguishes between following a 'just' Imam, where the previous prayer is treated as voluntary, and a non-just Imam, where the worshipper builds upon the existing prayer by adding one rak'ah while sitting in dissimulation (taqiyyah). The ruling emphasizes the flexibility of taqiyyah, noting that the worshipper is rewarded for it regardless of the specific method chosen.
